title: AI-Assisted Microbiome Analysis
text:

Explore a worked example using 24 synthetic samples, then apply the workflow to your own data.

New to the project? Start here.

title: Start here
text:
1. Choose how to begin
Question: How do community composition and diversity vary between two groups?
Inputs: 24 synthetic samples, 12 per group, and 15 fictional features.
Finish with: composition, diversity, and count-total figures; checked tables; a short report.
To explore without installing software, open the finished example report.
To reproduce the analysis or use your own data, complete the setup below. You need R, Quarto, and a text editor such as VS Code or RStudio.

title: Start here
text:
2. Open the project root
Download and extract the repository, then open ai-assisted-microbiome-analysis/ in your editor. This is the folder containing _quarto.yml, renv.lock, data/, and scripts/.
Open a terminal in that folder. Run every command in this guide from this root, including commands for chapters stored inside examples/.

title: Start here
text:
3. Restore the R environment
In the terminal, start R:
R
At the R prompt (>), run:
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org"))
if (!requireNamespace("renv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("renv")
}
renv::restore()
renv::status()
If asked to proceed, enter Y and wait for the > prompt before entering another command. The supplied lockfile records the project’s packages; learners restore it rather than initialize a new environment.
Check that the analysis packages load:
library(tidyverse)
library(vegan)
q(save = "no")






Note



If setup fails: stop and copy the error message. Resolve it before continuing. Ask AI to explain the error, then check its advice against your R version and operating system. Do not overwrite the lockfile to bypass an installation failure.

title: Start here
text:
4. Run and inspect the example
Back in the terminal, run:
Rscript scripts/R/01-check-inputs.R
Rscript scripts/R/02-analyse-example.R
The first command should report Input checks passed. The second saves tables in results/tables/ and three figures in results/figures/.
To view your local book:
quarto render
quarto preview
Rendering displays the results; it does not run the analysis scripts.

title: Start here
section: 5. Apply the workflow to your data
text:
5. Apply the workflow to your data
Keep the synthetic example intact. Create data/my-study/ containing:

feature-counts.tsv: feature IDs and sample count columns.
sample-metadata.tsv: sample IDs and group labels.
taxonomy.tsv: feature IDs and taxon labels.

Follow Meet the data for the required structure, then run:
Rscript scripts/R/02-analyse-example.R data/my-study results/my-study
This command validates your inputs before analysis and saves your outputs separately. Use Check the inputs to understand what validation covers.

Human → AI → Human
You define the comparison. AI helps explain code, investigate errors, and review drafts. You check the figures and calculations, decide what the evidence supports, and write the conclusion.







Note



Teaching scope: the example is synthetic and descriptive. Reusing the scripts requires checking that the methods suit your study design. Visual differences alone do not establish significance or causation.

title: Example report: two synthetic communities
text:
Question and inputs
How do community composition and diversity differ between two groups? This synthetic dataset contains 24 samples, 12 per group, and 15 fictional features. Feature-table totals range from 3299 to 11964. These totals are not verified raw sequencing depth.
crumbs: 4  Example report: two synthetic communities

title: Example report: two synthetic communities
text:
Methods
Validate identifiers and counts, calculate sample feature proportions, observed richness, and Shannon diversity using natural logarithms. The composition display retains the top eight features by mean sample proportion; all others become Other. Diversity uses all 15 features. No inferential tests are performed.

title: Example report: two synthetic communities
text:
Verification
A01 contains 6006 feature counts and 15 observed features. Dividing counts by the total and calculating \(-\sum p_i\ln(p_i)\) over positive proportions gives 2.423797. Every sample’s feature proportions sum to one.
Included tables were independently calculated from the counts. R execution and Quarto rendering were unavailable during this update; rerun both locally and compare numerical outputs before accepting the report.

title: Example report: two synthetic communities
text:
Limits and conclusion






Note



These are synthetic data. Higher diversity does not imply better health, and visual group differences do not establish significance or causation. Real studies require review of sampling effort, filtering, contamination, study design, and suitable statistical methods.

Use your own data
Create the same three filenames in data/my-study/. Use unique matching identifiers and untransformed integer counts, not percentages. Additional metadata are retained, but the scripts do not adjust for them.

title: Run the analysis
text:
Use your own data
Rscript scripts/R/02-analyse-example.R data/my-study results/my-study
The same script uses your identifiers and group labels, with no example-specific numeric values.

Full data for calculations; simplified data for display. The composition plot shows the top eight features by mean sample proportion and combines the rest as Other. Diversity uses every feature.

title: Run the analysis
text:
Check before continuing
Check sample counts, proportions summing to one, count totals, and labels. These are descriptive results; no significance tests are performed. For very large studies, review plot readability and computing resources.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Your task
Verify sample A01 from the count table.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Feature total: 6006.
Observed features: 15.
Shannon diversity: 2.423797.

x <- read.delim("data/example/feature-counts.tsv", check.names = FALSE)
p <- x$A01 / sum(x$A01)
-sum(p[p > 0] * log(p[p > 0]))

title: Verify and explain
text:

The calculation agrees with alpha-diversity.tsv. Repeat with a sample from your own study using its actual column name.

title: Verify and explain
text:
Explain the figures

What varies within and between groups?
Do diversity values overlap?
Could count totals, filtering, or study design affect interpretation?
Which claims cannot be supported?

Ask AI to review your draft against the tables. Verify each suggested claim yourself and record the check in results/decision-log.md.






Note



Higher diversity does not automatically mean a healthier community. Visual differences do not establish significance or causation.

title: Appendix A — Technical appendix
text:
Requirements
R, Quarto, and the packages recorded in root renv.lock. Restore with renv::restore(). The domain uses one shared environment.

title: Appendix A — Technical appendix
text:
Reuse
Both scripts accept optional input and output directories. Run from the repository root. Keep original study data separate from data/example/.
Feature tables must contain integer counts. Metadata must include sample_id and group; taxonomy must include matching feature_id and nonblank taxon. Zero-total samples fail validation.

title: Appendix A — Technical appendix
text:
Scope
The workflow starts from a feature table. It does not process raw reads, assign taxonomy, test group significance, adjust for repeated measures or confounding, or perform differential abundance analysis.
Included preview figures and tables were computed independently with Python. Run the supplied R scripts to regenerate equivalent numerical summaries and R-styled figures. Quarto code fences do not execute analysis.
